title: Trump Removes Rex Tillerson and Nominates Mike Pompeo as Secretary of State
description_short: Trump removed Rex Tillerson as Secretary of State and nominated CIA Director Mike Pompeo to replace him.
description_medium: On March 13, 2018, Donald Trump removed Rex Tillerson as Secretary of State and nominated CIA Director Mike Pompeo to succeed him. Contemporaneous reporting described months of policy disagreement, while archived White House material confirms Pompeo’s nomination. A later official transcript records a reporter’s timing claim about Tillerson’s Russia remarks but does not prove retaliation. This account describes the leadership change without asserting cronyism or obstruction.
description_long: On March 13, 2018, President Donald Trump removed Rex Tillerson as Secretary of State and nominated CIA Director Mike Pompeo to succeed him. A contemporaneous Washington Post report described months of disagreement and reported that Trump cited policy-strategy differences. The White House archive’s March 14 roundup of reactions identifies Pompeo as Trump’s nominee; a March 26 archived press-call transcript later records a reporter saying Tillerson was fired one day after strongly criticizing Russia over the Salisbury poisoning. The transcript does not establish that the Russia dispute caused the personnel change: the reporter framed the timing, while a senior administration official referred questions about the President’s conversations with Prime Minister Theresa May to the White House and did not explain Tillerson’s departure. The evidence supports a leadership change amid reported policy disagreements, but not a corrupt exchange, favoritism, obstruction, or a proven retaliatory motive. This proposal therefore describes the documented personnel action and leaves the existing category and subcategory unchanged for separate review.
